details: Multi-Turn Programming Benchmark, a benchmark consisting of 115 diverse problem sets that are factorized into multi-turn prompts

explainer.lead: MTPB is the Multi-Turn Programming Benchmark: 115 diverse problem sets factorised into multi-turn prompts. It matters for evaluating models on coding tasks that unfold across several conversational turns.

tiers.eli5: Instead of one big coding question, the test breaks each problem into several follow-up requests, checking whether the model can keep up as the conversation develops.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to assess how well a coding model handles evolving, multi-turn instructions rather than single-shot prompts; the pitfall is that performance can drop as context accumulates across turns.
tiers.paperLevel: MTPB is a benchmark consisting of 115 diverse problem sets that are factorised into multi-turn prompts, so each problem is evaluated through a sequence of turns rather than a single prompt.

explainer.example: A single programming task is decomposed into successive prompts — first specify the function, then add edge-case handling — and the model is scored on its responses across that sequence.
